heading: New Mexico Paycheck Calculator

parts.markdown:
Use our free New Mexico paycheck calculator to estimate your take-home pay after federal income tax, New Mexico income tax, Social Security, Medicare and other payroll deductions.

Enter your annual salary or hourly wage, choose your payment frequency and customize your withholding information to understand how much money you could receive on payday.

New Mexico uses progressive income tax withholding schedules, meaning your tax deduction depends on your earnings, payment frequency and applicable withholding classification.

Whether you work in Albuquerque, Santa Fe, Las Cruces, Rio Rancho or another New Mexico community, understanding your net earnings can help you compare salaries, manage household expenses and make informed financial decisions.

## How to Use the New Mexico Paycheck Calculator

Begin by selecting whether you receive annual salary or hourly wages.

Enter your gross income before taxes. Hourly employees should provide their regular working hours and qualifying overtime hours.

Select your payment frequency. Enter federal and New Mexico income tax withheld for the pay period from your pay stub, including any extra withholding.

Include retirement contributions, health insurance premiums and other employee deductions.

If your earnings are approaching an annual payroll contribution ceiling, enter your year-to-date taxable wages.

Review your estimated paycheck breakdown to understand how individual deductions affect your remaining take-home income.

For greater accuracy, use information from your most recent payroll statement rather than estimating your benefit deductions.

## New Mexico Payroll Taxes in 2026

New Mexico employees generally encounter the following payroll taxes.

New Mexico's state withholding calculation includes different wage thresholds according to payment frequency and withholding classification.

The [New Mexico Taxation and Revenue Department](https://www.tax.newmexico.gov/) publishes official employer withholding guidance.

## How New Mexico State Income Tax Works

New Mexico applies progressive individual income tax rates.

Instead of taxing all earnings at one percentage, the system applies different rates to different portions of applicable income.

The 2026 payroll percentage schedules include rates of 1.5%, 3.2%, 4.3%, 4.7%, 4.9% and 5.9%, alongside applicable zero-withholding ranges.

However, these rates cannot be applied accurately without considering the corresponding thresholds and base withholding amounts.

An employee whose highest applicable marginal withholding rate is 4.7% does not necessarily have 4.7% deducted from their entire gross salary.

Employers follow the applicable percentage tables or other authorized procedures in the state's wage withholding publication.

## Understanding New Mexico Withholding Tables

New Mexico publishes its state wage withholding tables in Publication FYI-104.

The tables are organized according to payroll frequency and applicable withholding classification.

For example, weekly employees use a different table from employees receiving biweekly or monthly paychecks.

The tables incorporate wage thresholds and base withholding amounts. These features help employers calculate the appropriate deduction without requiring employees to perform a complete annual income tax calculation every payday.

Read the official [New Mexico withholding tax publication FYI-104](https://www.tax.newmexico.gov/businesses/wage-withholding-tax/) for employer calculation guidance.

Always confirm that the publication applies to the correct tax year before using its tables.

## Why Filing Status Affects New Mexico Take-Home Pay

An employee's applicable withholding classification influences the wage thresholds used to calculate New Mexico income tax withholding.

Single, married and head-of-household classifications generally have different thresholds.

Consequently, two employees receiving the same gross salary may have different state tax deductions.

Married employees with multiple household income sources should review their withholding selections carefully.

If both spouses receive wages, their combined withholding may not necessarily cover their final household tax liability.

Employees should also distinguish federal withholding adjustments from state withholding requirements. A change to federal tax credits does not necessarily produce an identical change in New Mexico withholding.

## Federal Taxes Deducted From New Mexico Paychecks


### Federal income tax

Your employer generally calculates federal income tax withholding using your taxable wages, filing status, payment frequency and information supplied on Form W-4.

Multiple jobs, eligible credits, other income and additional withholding requests may affect your deduction.

The [IRS federal withholding methods](https://www.irs.gov/publications/p15t) provide official calculation instructions.

### Social Security

Employees generally contribute 6.2% of covered wages toward Social Security.

The annual taxable wage ceiling is $184,500 in 2026.

For example, an employee receiving $2,000 in covered wages before reaching the annual limit would contribute $124.

### Medicare

Ordinary Medicare withholding applies at 1.45% of covered wages.

An employee receiving $2,000 in Medicare-covered wages would ordinarily contribute $29.

Employers generally withhold an additional 0.9% on covered Medicare wages exceeding $200,000 paid by that employer during the calendar year.

Review the [IRS Employer's Tax Guide](https://www.irs.gov/publications/p15) for further information.

## New Mexico Paycheck Example: $65,000 Salary

Consider an employee earning $65,000 annually before taxes and deductions.
Assume the employee receives $2,500 biweekly, uses ordinary single federal withholding settings and has no additional federal credits, income adjustments or employee benefit deductions.

Approximately $2,092.60 remains before New Mexico income tax and other employee deductions.

To complete the paycheck calculation, subtract applicable New Mexico withholding and any other deductions.

For illustration, if your actual New Mexico withholding were $85 and other post-tax deductions totaled $40, your resulting net paycheck would be $1,967.60.

The $85 figure is hypothetical, not a calculated 2026 New Mexico withholding amount. Use the applicable state tables and your actual withholding information for a personalized estimate.

## New Mexico Hourly Paycheck Calculator

Hourly employees can estimate gross earnings using their hourly wage, working hours and qualifying overtime.

Suppose an employee earns $26 per hour and works 40 regular hours plus six overtime hours paid at time-and-a-half.

Regular earnings:

$26 × 40 = $1,040

Overtime earnings:

$26 × 1.5 × 6 = $234

Total gross earnings:

$1,274

Federal income tax, New Mexico income tax and applicable payroll contributions are then calculated from their respective taxable wage amounts.

Employees receiving shift differentials, tips, commissions or bonuses may experience different paycheck amounts throughout the year.

Consult the [New Mexico Department of Workforce Solutions](https://www.dws.state.nm.us/) and the [US Department of Labor overtime guidance](https://www.dol.gov/agencies/whd/overtime) for applicable employment requirements.

## Does Albuquerque Have a Local Income Tax?

Albuquerque and other New Mexico municipalities generally do not impose separate personal wage income taxes on ordinary employee compensation.

New Mexico's gross receipts tax is different from personal income tax withholding.

Gross receipts tax may affect the price of goods and services, while business owners and independent contractors can have separate tax obligations.

An ordinary W-2 employee should not automatically have gross receipts tax deducted from wages as though it were an individual payroll income tax.

Visit the New Mexico Taxation and Revenue Department for information about the distinction between personal income tax and business taxation.

## Working Across New Mexico State Borders

New Mexico shares borders with Texas, Arizona, Colorado, Oklahoma and Utah.

Employees who live in one state and perform employment duties in another may have different withholding obligations.

For example, living in Texas, which does not impose individual state wage income tax, does not automatically exempt wages earned through employment in New Mexico.

The appropriate tax treatment depends on residency, the location where work is performed and applicable state rules.

Certain employment arrangements involving tribal lands or qualifying Native American income tax exemptions may also require specialized treatment.

A standard New Mexico paycheck calculator should not be treated as a complete multi-jurisdiction or tribal tax estimator.

## How Employee Benefits Affect New Mexico Take-Home Pay

Your employer may deduct retirement contributions, healthcare premiums, dental insurance and other employee benefits.

Traditional retirement contributions generally reduce current federal income-taxable wages. Roth contributions generally do not provide the same immediate income tax reduction.

Qualifying health insurance arrangements may reduce certain taxable wage amounts.

Other deductions reduce your net paycheck without necessarily reducing applicable payroll taxes.

For this reason, a reliable calculator must distinguish between deductions that affect income-taxable wages and deductions that are taken after taxes.

Compare your estimated paycheck with your actual payroll statement to identify differences in benefit treatment.

## Managing Your New Mexico Take-Home Income

Build your monthly budget using estimated net earnings rather than annual gross salary.

Account for housing, transportation, groceries, utilities, healthcare and required debt payments.

Employees working in energy, tourism or seasonal industries should also consider periods when overtime or working hours may decline.

Our [emergency fund calculator](/savings/emergency-fund-calculator/) can help establish an appropriate savings target, while our [salary-to-hourly calculator](/calculators/salary-to-hourly-calculator/) can help compare fixed salaries with hourly employment.

When comparing job offers, consider employer retirement matching, insurance premiums and commuting costs alongside take-home pay.

## Frequently Asked Questions


### What is New Mexico's income tax rate in 2026?

New Mexico uses progressive income tax rates ranging from 1.5% to 5.9%, with applicable zero-withholding thresholds. Actual paycheck withholding depends on the relevant official payroll schedule.

### Does Albuquerque have a separate employee income tax?

Albuquerque generally does not impose a separate personal wage income tax. Applicable federal and New Mexico income taxes still affect employee earnings.

### Why is my New Mexico paycheck different from the calculator?

Differences can arise from withholding classifications, benefit deductions, employer rounding, supplemental compensation or employment circumstances not included in a standard estimate.

The results are educational estimates rather than official payroll calculations or individualized tax advice.
